zones.name: Florida freshwater
zones.description: Statewide freshwater limits. Individual lakes, rivers and Fish Management Areas can have their own rules.
notes: The FWC statewide limits page lists no closed season for black bass. Some waters have their own limits or permits, so check FWC for the water you plan to fish.

regs.title: Freshwater limits

rows.label: Black bass
rows.value: 5 per day in total, any mix of Florida, largemouth, Suwannee, spotted, Choctaw and shoal bass. Only one may be 16 inches or longer.

rows.label: Largemouth
rows.value: No minimum length.

rows.label: Suwannee, shoal, spotted, Choctaw bass
rows.value: 12 inch minimum. Do not kill or possess one under 12 inches.

rows.label: Crappie (speckled perch)
rows.value: 25 per day.

rows.label: Sunfish (panfish)
rows.value: 50 per day in total (bluegill, redear, flier, longear and others).

rows.label: Striped, white and sunshine bass
rows.value: 20 per day in total, only 6 may be 24 inches or longer.

rows.label: Butterfly peacock bass
rows.value: 2 per day, only one may be 17 inches or longer.

rows.label: Catfish and other nongame fish
rows.value: No bag or possession limit, except where a Fish Management Area sets one.

rows.label: Grass carp, alligator gar
rows.value: Release at once. You may not possess them without a permit.

rows.label: Shoal bass, Chipola River
rows.value: Release every shoal bass at once on the Chipola River and its tributaries.

rows.label: Suwannee bass, Wakulla River
rows.value: Release at once on the Wakulla River, from the headsprings to the St. Marks River.

rows.label: Keeping bass whole
rows.value: Black bass may not be filleted or have the head or tail fin removed until you finish fishing for the day.

notes: FWC states there are no new freshwater regulation changes for 2026-27.
Rules for a particular lake, river or Fish Management Area can differ. Check FWC before you keep fish.
Licence rules for borderline tidal or brackish waters are not spelled out on the FWC pages: Check FWC.

For the exact closed-area boundary, see rule 68B-31.008, Florida Administrative Code. The FWC shrimp page still names the repealed rule 68B-31.017.

regs.title: Shrimping rules

rows.label: License
rows.value: Recreational saltwater fishing license, unless exempt.

rows.label: Limit
rows.value: 5 gallons heads-on per harvester, never more than 5 gallons per vessel. Big Bend region: 2 gallons per person, 5 per vessel.

rows.label: Possession
rows.value: 5 gallons heads-on per vessel at any time, however many people are aboard.

rows.label: Nets
rows.value: No more than two nets fished from one vessel at a time.

rows.label: Dip or landing net
rows.value: Opening no larger than 96 inches around the perimeter.

rows.label: Cast net
rows.value: Stretched length no more than 14 feet.

rows.label: Push net, beach seine
rows.value: Push net pushed by a person wading. Haul seine up to 500 square feet, stretched mesh up to 2 inches, not monofilament.

rows.label: Frame net
rows.value: Opening up to 16 feet around, from a vessel or a structure other than a bridge, not monofilament, not towed, not in Miami-Dade County.

rows.label: Traps
rows.value: Up to four, each no larger than 36 x 24 x 12 inches.

rows.label: Bait poles (cast net)
rows.value: Up to five non-metal poles, set at least 10 yards apart and not within 50 yards of docks, ramps, seawalls, jetties or bridges. Daylight only.

rows.label: Northeast closure
rows.value: April 1 to May 31, inside waters of Nassau, Duval, St. Johns, Putnam, Flagler and Clay counties.

rows.label: Apalachicola Bay
rows.value: Part closed Mar 1 to May 31 and Sep 15 to Dec 31. All of the bay and St. Vincent Sound closed sunrise to sunset, Jul 15 to Sep 14.

notes: Rules for lights, specific rivers and bridges are not stated on the FWC page: Check FWC.
Contact your nearest FWC law enforcement office for local restrictions.

zones.toxinAdvisory: Closed for toxin-producing algae. FWC reopens the zone only when tests show levels are safe. The area stays open for fishing, boating and swimming.
notes: The 2026 Pasco season opened July 10 and was set to run through August 18 (FWC news release, July 10, 2026). It closed early on August 6.

regs.title: Scallop rules

rows.label: Per person
rows.value: 2 gallons whole in the shell, or 1 pint of meat.

rows.label: Per vessel
rows.value: 10 gallons whole, or 1/2 gallon (4 pints) of meat. A vessel limit never lets one person take more than the personal limit.

rows.label: Fenholloway to Suwannee, June 15 to 30
rows.value: 1 gallon whole or 1 cup shucked per person, 5 gallons or 2 pints shucked per vessel.

rows.label: Size
rows.value: No minimum size.

rows.label: How to take
rows.value: By hand or with a landing (dip) net only. No commercial harvest.

rows.label: License
rows.value: Recreational saltwater license unless exempt. The no-cost shoreline license covers wading from shore only: no swimming, snorkeling or SCUBA, and no vessel.

rows.label: Closed zones
rows.value: You may carry legally harvested scallops through a closed area.

rows.label: Shells
rows.value: Do not dump shells in inshore waters used for recreation such as the Homosassa and Crystal rivers. Use a trash receptacle or larger waters.

notes: Zones can close by FWC order with little notice. Check FWC the morning you go.
2027 dates are not announced yet.

zones.name: Florida (except Monroe County and Biscayne National Park)
zones.description: Regular season August 6 to March 31, plus the two-day sport season.
notes: Daily bag: 6 per person in the regular season, 12 per person in the sport season.

zones.name: Monroe County and Biscayne National Park
zones.description: Same season dates. A lower sport-season bag, and night diving is prohibited in Monroe County during the sport season.
notes: Daily bag: 6 per person in both the regular and the sport season.
John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park is closed to harvest during the sport season.

regs.title: Lobster rules

rows.label: Regular season
rows.value: August 6 to March 31. 6 per person per day.

rows.label: Sport season
rows.value: Last consecutive Wednesday and Thursday of July: July 28 and 29, 2027. 12 per person per day, but 6 per person in Monroe County and Biscayne National Park.

rows.label: Possession
rows.value: On the water: the daily bag. Off the water in the sport season: one day's bag on day one, double on day two. Limits are enforced on and off the water.

rows.label: Size
rows.value: Carapace longer than 3 inches, measured in the water. Carry and use a measuring device at all times.

rows.label: Egg-bearing
rows.value: Egg-bearing spiny, slipper and furry lobsters may not be taken or kept.

rows.label: Whole only
rows.value: Land lobster whole. Separating the tail from the body is prohibited in state waters.

rows.label: License and permit
rows.value: Recreational saltwater license and a lobster permit, unless exempt.

rows.label: Allowed gear
rows.value: Landing or dip net, bully net up to 3 feet across, hoop net up to 10 feet across.

rows.label: Not allowed
rows.value: Any device that could puncture, penetrate or crush the lobster, bleach or other chemicals, artificial habitat, and traps.

rows.label: Night diving
rows.value: Prohibited in Monroe County during the sport season only.

rows.label: No harvest, all year
rows.value: Everglades National Park, Dry Tortugas National Park, no-take areas of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary, Biscayne Bay/Card Sound Lobster Sanctuary, and the five Coral Reef Protection Areas in Biscayne National Park.

rows.label: No harvest, sport season
rows.value: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park.

notes: Bag limits count only licensed people who are harvesting.
The FWC lobster page does not mention a dive flag. Florida law requires a divers-down flag for divers and snorkelers (Florida Statute 327.331).

Spotted seatrout rules differ by region (FWC, since April 1, 2026). Indian River Lagoon region: closed November 1 to December 31, 2 fish. Panhandle: closed in February. Big Bend: 5 fish. Rest of the state 3 fish. The rule shown here is for Tampa Bay; check your region on MyFWC.com.

Red snapper dates differ by coast (FWC). The dates shown are for the Gulf. Atlantic (east coast and Keys Atlantic side): closed now, the 2026 season Oct. 9 to 22 is over. Check MyFWC.com if you fish the Atlantic.

Gag grouper rules differ by coast (FWC). The dates shown are for the Gulf (open Sept. 1-30, 2026). Atlantic and the Keys: 1 gag or black per person, combined 2 per vessel, no for-hire crew bag, 2026 season May 1 to Aug. 1 (over). Check MyFWC.com.

Black grouper rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic and the Keys: closed Jan. 1 to April 30, 1 gag or black per person, combined 2 per vessel, no for-hire crew bag. Check MyFWC.com.
Red grouper rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic and the Keys: closed Jan. 1 to April 30, up to 3 per person within the 3-grouper aggregate. Check MyFWC.com.
Scamp rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic and the Keys: 20 in, closed Jan. 1 to April 30, up to 3 per person within the 3-grouper aggregate. Check MyFWC.com.
Red hind rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic and the Keys: closed Jan. 1 to April 30, up to 3 per person within the 3-grouper aggregate. Check MyFWC.com.
Rock hind rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic and the Keys: closed Jan. 1 to April 30, up to 3 per person within the 3-grouper aggregate. Check MyFWC.com.
Hogfish rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. South of Cape Sable (the Keys) and the Atlantic coast: 16 in, 1 fish, open May 1 to Oct. 31 only. Check MyFWC.com.
Gray triggerfish rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic: 12 in, up to 10 per person, open all year. Check MyFWC.com.
Greater amberjack rules differ by coast (FWC). The dates shown are for the Gulf (open Sept. 1 to Oct. 13, 2026). Atlantic: 28 in, 1 fish, closed April only. Check MyFWC.com.
Vermilion snapper rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic: 12 in, 5 per person. Check MyFWC.com.
Lane snapper rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic: 8 in, 10 per person within the snapper aggregate. Check MyFWC.com.
Black sea bass rules differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown is for the Gulf. Atlantic: 13 in, 7 per person. Check MyFWC.com.
King mackerel bag limits differ by coast (FWC). The rule shown (3 per person) is for the Gulf and the Keys. Atlantic state waters north of Monroe County: 2 per person. Check MyFWC.com.

Snook seasons differ by FWC region. The rule shown is for the Tampa Bay region (closed Dec. 1 to end of Feb. and May 1 to Aug. 31, 28 to 33 in). Atlantic coast (Southeast, Indian River, Northeast): closed Dec. 15 to Jan. 31 and June 1 to Aug. 31, 28 to 32 in. Southwest and Charlotte Harbor: closed May 1 to Sept. 30. Check MyFWC.com.

Redfish rules differ by FWC region. The rule shown is for the Tampa Bay region (1 fish, 18 to 27 in, 2-fish vessel limit). Indian River Lagoon (Sebastian to Stuart): catch and release only. Panhandle, Big Bend and Northeast: 4-fish vessel limit. Check MyFWC.com.
